title: Present Perfect: have + past participle
grammarNote:
Present Perfect СОЕДИНЯЕТ прошлое с настоящим. Думаем о РЕЗУЛЬТАТЕ сейчас, а не о времени когда это произошло.

① Жизненный опыт (ever/never):
   "I have visited Almaty." (был → имею этот опыт)
   "She has never eaten sushi." (никогда не пробовала)
   "Have you ever tried skiing?"

② Только что завершилось (just/already/yet):
   "I have just finished my homework." (только что)
   "She has already sent the email." (уже)
   "Have you done your project yet?" (уже / ещё нет?)

③ Началось в прошлом и продолжается сейчас (for/since):
   "I have lived in Uralsk for 5 years." (живу и сейчас!)

🔧 Образование: have/has + PAST PARTICIPLE
Regular: work→worked, study→studied
Irregular: go→gone, see→seen, write→written, do→done

⚠️ Отличие от Past Simple:
"I visited Astana last year." (конкретное время)
"I have visited Astana." (опыт, время не важно)

grammarTable.subject: NEGATIVE: I / You / We / They
grammarTable.example: I haven't been to Edinburgh yet.

grammarTable.subject: NEGATIVE: He / She / It
grammarTable.example: She hasn't heard back from Edinburgh.

grammarTable.subject: QUESTION: Have + I/you/we/they
grammarTable.example: Have you ever been to the Altai?

grammarTable.subject: SHORT ANSWER positive
grammarTable.example: Have you tried it? — Yes, I have.

grammarTable.subject: SHORT ANSWER negative
grammarTable.example: Has she been? — No, she hasn't.

rows.form: Regular verbs: base + -ed (same as Past Simple)
rows.example: visit → visited, try → tried, live → lived, play → played

rows.form: Irregular Group 1: different past, different participle
rows.example: go → went → gone;  see → saw → seen;  do → did → done

rows.form: Irregular Group 2: past = participle
rows.example: have → had → had;  make → made → made;  buy → bought → bought

rows.form: Irregular Group 3: all three forms different
rows.example: write → wrote → written;  take → took → taken;  give → gave → given

rows.form: Irregular Group 4: base = participle (not past)
rows.example: come → came → come;  run → ran → run;  become → became → become

rows.form: Key ones to memorise
rows.example: be → been, eat → eaten, speak → spoken, break → broken, choose → chosen

grammarExtra.title: Three Main Uses of Present Perfect

rows.form: Use 1: Life experience (ever/never) — no specific time
rows.example: Have you ever tried Kazakh food? / I've never seen the Northern Lights.

rows.form: Use 2: Recent event — result matters now (just/recently)
rows.example: She's just arrived. / He's recently started a new job. (the result = they are now here/employed)

rows.form: Use 3: Unfinished time period (for/since)
rows.example: She has lived here for 3 years. / He has studied English since 2020. (still happening now)

rows.form: Connecting word: already (sooner than expected)
rows.example: I've already finished my homework! (earlier than expected)

rows.form: Connecting word: yet (expected but not done)
rows.example: I haven't packed yet. / Have you booked yet?

rows.form: Connecting word: just (very recently)
rows.example: She's just called me. / He's just left the building.

grammarExtra.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Key Rule

rows.form: Present Perfect: no specific past time mentioned
rows.example: I have visited Almaty. (some time in my life — not specified)

rows.form: Past Simple: specific past time mentioned
rows.example: I visited Almaty in 2022. / I visited Almaty last summer.

rows.form: The "time word" test
rows.example: yesterday / last week / in 2020 / three days ago → Past Simple ONLY

rows.form: Vague time → Present Perfect OK
rows.example: recently / before / ever / never / so far / already / just / yet → Present Perfect

rows.form: Follow-up question after Present Perfect → Past Simple
rows.example: Have you been to Paris? — Yes! / When did you go? — I went in 2019.

rows.form: Common mistake: "I have gone there yesterday." ✗
rows.example: Correct: "I went there yesterday." (yesterday = specific → Past Simple)

grammarExtra.title: for vs since — Duration vs Start Point

rows.form: for + period of time (duration)
rows.example: She has studied English for three years. / He has lived here for six months.

rows.form: since + point in time (start)
rows.example: She has studied English since 2021. / He has lived here since January.

rows.form: Quick test: "for" answers "How long?" and "since" answers "Since when?"
rows.example: How long? — for 3 years. Since when? — since 2021.

rows.form: for + number + time unit
rows.example: for two weeks, for six months, for a long time, for five years

rows.form: since + specific point
rows.example: since Monday, since 1990, since I was a child, since she arrived

rows.form: Both with Present Perfect (not Past Simple)
rows.example: She has lived here for 3 years. ✓ / She lived here for 3 years. ✗ (if still true now)

grammarTip:
Самый простой способ выбрать Past Simple или Present Perfect:

❓ Знаешь конкретное время? → PAST SIMPLE
"I visited Astana LAST SUMMER." → Past Simple
"She called me YESTERDAY." → Past Simple

❓ Время не важно / опыт / результат сейчас? → PRESENT PERFECT
"I have visited Astana." (просто был — когда? не важно)

Сигналы:
Past Simple: yesterday, last week, in 2020, ago, when I was...
Present Perfect: ever, never, already, just, yet, recently, for, since

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct Present Perfect form.
Write the correct Present Perfect form.
exercises.hint: I → "have" + never + past participle. "See" → past participle is "seen".
Question: Have + you + ever + past participle. "Be" → past participle is "been".

exercises.instruction: Choose Present Perfect or Past Simple.
exercises.hint: "In 2022" is a specific time → Past Simple.
"For five years" with an ongoing activity → Present Perfect: has played.

exercises.text: Zhibek has volunteered at the hospital ___ two years.
exercises.hint: "Two years" = a period of time → use "for".

exercises.text: ___ Rustam ever ___ (get) lost on a hiking trip?
exercises.hint: Question about experience: Has + he/she + ever + past participle. "Get" → past participle = "got".

exercises.instruction: Choose Present Perfect or Past Simple.
exercises.text: I ___ the email. I received it just now.
exercises.hint: "Just" (very recently) → Present Perfect: have/has + just + past participle.

exercises.text: She has studied English ___ she was fourteen.
exercises.hint: "She was fourteen" = a point in time → use "since".

exercises.text: I ___ my homework yet. I'll do it tonight.
exercises.hint: "Yet" signals something expected but not done → Present Perfect negative: haven't + past participle.

exercises.instruction: Which sentence is in Present Perfect?
exercises.hint: Present Perfect = has/have + past participle. "Has visited" is the correct form.

exercises.text: "Have you ever tried skydiving?" — "___, I have. It was incredible!"
exercises.hint: Short answer to "Have you ever...?": Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.

questions.text: She ___ five items off her bucket list.
questions.hint: She = third person singular → "has" + past participle (crossed).

questions.text: I ___ (never / be) to the Altai Mountains.
questions.hint: "I" → have + never + past participle. "Be" → past participle is "been".
"Has" + he + ever + past participle. "Sleep" → past participle = "slept".

questions.text: "I have gone there yesterday" is correct.
questions.hint: "Yesterday" = specific time → must use Past Simple: "I went there yesterday."
"Just" = very recently → Present Perfect: has + just + past participle.

questions.text: They ___ the report yet. They're still working on it.
questions.hint: "Yet" with a negative → Present Perfect: haven't + past participle.

questions.text: What is the past participle of "write"?
questions.hint: write → wrote → written (completely irregular: base / past / participle).

questions.text: He has lived in Uralsk ___ five years.
Present Perfect can be used with "last year" and "yesterday".
questions.hint: "Last year" and "yesterday" are specific times → use Past Simple, not Present Perfect.

questions.text: Have you ever ___ a traditional meal?
questions.hint: Present Perfect: have + ever + past participle. "Cook" → past participle is "cooked".

questions.text: ___ she ___ (see) the Northern Lights? — No, she ___.
questions.hint: Question: Has + she + past participle? Short negative answer: No, she hasn't.

questions.text: I've ___ finished my essay — I sent it five minutes ago.
questions.hint: "Already" = sooner than expected → present perfect: "I've already finished."

questions.text: What is the past participle of "take"?
Which sentence correctly uses Present Perfect?
opts: She has called me last night.
questions.hint: "Yesterday" = specific time → Past Simple. Present Perfect cannot be used with "yesterday".
